channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation "users" does not exist
item.description: Postgres could not find the table in the database the repo is connected to. Usually migrations have not run in this environment: the test database is migrated separately from dev, and a release does not run migrations when it starts. Otherwise you are connected to a different database than you…

item.title: Alertmanager: undefined receiver "slack-ops" used in route
item.description: Every route in the Alertmanager config names a receiver, and the name must match a receivers entry exactly, case included. This is checked when the file loads, so on startup Alertmanager refuses to run, and on a reload it quietly keeps the previous config: alerts carry on going to the old place…

item.title: Ansible: Could not find or access 'nginx.conf.j2'
item.description: The copy, template or script module looked for its source file on the control node and could not find it. A relative src is resolved against the role's files/ or templates/ directory, or the playbook's own directory, not the directory you ran the command from, which is why the same path works in…

item.title: Ansible: ERROR! 'apt' is not a valid attribute for a Play
item.description: Ansible read a key at play level and it is not a play keyword such as hosts, become or tasks. Nearly always a module has been written straight under the play, the tasks: line is missing, or indentation has slipped so a task sits beside hosts instead of inside the list. Running a file of tasks…

item.title: Ansible: Unsupported parameters for (ansible.builtin.copy) module: dest_path
item.description: Every module checks its arguments against a fixed list before it runs, and one of yours is not on it. Typos and options borrowed from a similar module are common, but the confusing case is a version mismatch: the documentation you are reading describes a newer release of the module or collection…

item.title: atob: The string to be decoded is not correctly encoded
item.description: atob() only accepts standard Base64: letters, digits, + and /, padded with = to a multiple of four characters. The usual culprit is Base64url, which swaps + and / for - and _ and drops the padding, and is what JWTs, WebAuthn and plenty of APIs emit. A value that was URL-encoded on the way in (%2B…

item.title: AWS S3: AccessControlListNotSupported: The bucket does not allow ACLs
item.description: Since April 2023 new S3 buckets default to the 'Bucket owner enforced' Object Ownership setting, which switches ACLs off entirely. Any request that sets an ACL, such as the public-read that older tools, plugins and tutorials add by default, is refused, even though nothing about your permissions…

item.title: AWS S3: EntityTooLarge: Your proposed upload exceeds the maximum allowed size
item.description: A single PUT to S3 can carry at most 5 GB; anything bigger has to be a multipart upload. The AWS CLI and the SDK transfer managers switch to multipart on their own, so this usually comes from a raw PutObject call, a presigned PUT URL (always a single request), or a browser POST form whose policy…

item.title: C#: FormatException: Input string was not in a correct format
item.description: int.Parse, decimal.Parse, Convert.ToInt32 and friends throw this when the text is not a number in the format they expect. Empty strings and stray characters are the obvious causes. The one that works on your machine and fails on a server is culture: decimal.Parse("1.5") uses the current culture…

item.title: C#: System.InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no elements
item.description: A LINQ operator that has to return a value found nothing to return. First(), Single(), Last(), and Min(), Max() or Average() over a non-nullable type all throw on an empty sequence rather than make something up. With EF Core it usually means the filter matched no rows, often because an ID came…

item.title: Cargo: package `foo v1.2.3` cannot be built because it requires rustc 1.82
item.description: A dependency sets rust-version in its Cargo.toml (its minimum supported Rust version) and your toolchain is older. Edition 2024 projects resolve dependencies that suit their own rust-version, but older editions, an existing Cargo.lock, or a project with no rust-version will happily pick the newest…

item.title: Ecto: (Ecto.ConstraintError) constraint error when attempting to insert struct
item.description: The database rejected the insert on a unique, foreign key or check constraint, and the changeset had no matching *_constraint declared, so Ecto raised instead of returning {:error, changeset}. The message names the constraint and lists the ones the changeset does know about. Declaring…

item.title: EF Core: Cannot access a disposed context instance
item.description: The DbContext was disposed when its dependency injection scope ended, and something carried on using it. In ASP.NET Core that scope is the HTTP request, so anything that outlives the request trips it: an async void method, a Task started with Task.Run or never awaited, an IQueryable returned and…

item.title: Elixir: could not fetch application environment :api_key for application
item.description: Application.fetch_env!/2 raised because the key was never set for that application. Config files run at different times: config.exs and prod.exs at build time, runtime.exs at boot, so System.get_env in prod.exs reads the build machine's environment, not the server's. The other trap is fetch_env!…

item.title: Failed to read the 'localStorage' property from 'Window': Access is denied
item.description: Chrome throws this the moment code touches window.localStorage on a page where storage is blocked for that origin. The common case is your page running in an iframe on someone else's site with third-party cookies blocked; it also happens when the user blocks all site data, and in sandboxed iframes…

item.title: fetch: Request with GET/HEAD method cannot have body
item.description: The Fetch standard forbids a body on GET and HEAD requests, so the browser rejects the call before anything reaches the network. It usually comes from a shared wrapper that always attaches JSON, or from code ported from axios or curl that sent filters in a GET body, which some servers tolerate…

item.title: Fluentd: [warn]: #0 pattern not matched
item.description: A parser, usually a regexp on in_tail, could not match a line, so Fluentd logs a warning and drops it instead of emitting a record. When only some lines fail, they are typically continuation lines of a multiline stack trace, which need the multiline parser rather than a looser regex. When every…

item.title: GitHub Actions: No files were found with the provided path
item.description: actions/upload-artifact matched nothing, and by default it only warns and carries on, so the real failure shows up later when a download or deploy job finds nothing to work with. The path is relative to the workspace, not to the working-directory of an earlier run step. A build that wrote its…

item.title: GitHub Actions: Unable to resolve action `org/deploy@v3`, unable to find version
item.description: Before any step runs, the runner downloads every action named in uses:, and this one points at a tag, branch or commit that does not exist in that repository. Many actions keep a moving major tag such as v4 next to v4.2.1, but not all do, so a version copied from a README may only exist as a full…

item.title: GitHub Actions: Waiting for a runner to pick up this job...
item.description: The job is queued, but no available runner carries every label listed in runs-on, so GitHub keeps waiting instead of failing. A misspelt label never matches, and neither does a self-hosted runner that is offline, missing one of the labels, or in a runner group this repository is not allowed to…

item.title: Go: inconsistent vendoring
item.description: The project has a vendor directory, so the go command builds from it, but vendor/modules.txt no longer agrees with go.mod: a dependency was added, upgraded or removed without vendoring again. It often follows a Dependabot or Renovate pull request that only touched go.mod and go.sum, or a hand edit…

item.title: Go: panic: sync: negative WaitGroup counter
item.description: Done() was called more times than Add() allowed for, taking the counter below zero. Typical sources: Done both deferred and called explicitly, a goroutine that calls Done on an error path and again at the end, or Add placed inside the goroutine so retries and early returns throw the count off…

item.title: go: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/acme/lib/@v/list: 404 Not Found
item.description: By default Go fetches modules through the public proxy at proxy.golang.org and checks them against sum.golang.org. Neither can see a private repository, so the proxy answers 404 or 410, and when Go falls back to git directly it often ends with 'terminal prompts disabled'. The fix is not…

item.title: Jest: Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed.
item.description: The tests passed, but something they started is still holding Node's event loop open: a database pool, an HTTP server, a setInterval, an open socket. Jest waits for the process to drain and prints this instead of exiting, which in CI can mean the job hangs until it times out. --detectOpenHandles…

item.title: journald: system.journal corrupted or uncleanly shut down, renaming
item.description: journald found its active journal file was never marked as cleanly closed, so rather than trust it, it renamed the file with a ~ suffix and started a fresh one. After a power cut, a hard reset or journald being killed, that is expected and harmless, and the old file stays readable. If it happens…

item.title: Loki: ingestion rate limit exceeded for user fake (limit: 4194304 bytes/sec)
item.description: Loki enforces a per-tenant ingestion rate (4 MB/s by default, with a 6 MB burst) and rejects pushes over it with HTTP 429. 'fake' is just the tenant name Loki uses when auth is disabled. Promtail, Alloy and Fluent Bit retry with backoff, so a short spike costs nothing, but sustained overload means…

item.title: Prometheus: field scrape_config not found in type config.plain
item.description: Prometheus parses its YAML strictly, so a key it does not recognise is fatal: the server will not start, or a reload is rejected and the old config stays live. config.plain is the top level of the file, so the key is either misspelt (scrape_config for scrape_configs) or indented so that it lands…

item.title: Prometheus: query processing would load too many samples into memory
item.description: Prometheus caps how many samples one query may hold in memory at once (--query.max-samples, 50 million by default) and aborts the query rather than risk running out of memory. The limit counts samples touched, not rows returned, so a long range with a small step, a [30d] range vector over many…

item.title: pytest: PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.slow
item.description: pytest only knows marks that are built in, registered in config, or added by a plugin, so @pytest.mark.slow on its own is treated as a likely typo. It is worth fixing because a misspelt mark silently does nothing: -m "not slow" will happily run a test marked @pytest.mark.slwo. With…

item.title: React: An update to App inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)
item.description: React saw a state update land while a test was running but outside act(), which means your assertions may have run before React finished rendering. With Testing Library the cause is nearly always asynchronous work finishing after the test's last await: a fetch resolving, a timer firing, a setState…

item.title: rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors)
item.description: Code 23 is a summary, not the error. rsync finished, but at least one file or attribute could not be copied, and the real reason was printed earlier, often thousands of lines up. Usual causes: permission denied reading a source file, a destination that cannot store owners, groups or permissions…

item.description: The first part of a path, like serde_json in serde_json::to_string, is neither a dependency in Cargo.toml nor a module declared in this crate. Recent compilers word it 'use of unresolved module or unlinked crate'. The usual causes: the dependency is missing or only listed under dev-dependencies…

item.description: The method exists, but it belongs to a trait, and trait methods can only be called where the trait is imported. write_all comes from std::io::Write, read_to_string from std::io::Read, and many crates work the same way (tokio's AsyncWriteExt, rand's Rng). The compiler's help line saying a trait 'is…

item.title: Terraform: Error: Unsupported attribute
item.description: A reference such as aws_instance.web.public_ip or module.vpc.subnet_ids points at an attribute the object does not have. For resources it is usually a typo or something a provider renamed in a major version. For modules it is almost always a missing output: a module only exposes what it declares…

item.title: Terraform: Error: Unsupported Terraform Core version
item.description: A terraform block somewhere in the configuration sets required_version, and the binary you are running falls outside it. Every module is checked, including ones you did not write, so upgrading a registry module can bring this in without any change to your own code. It turns up most on CI runners…

item.title: Terraform: the "for_each" argument must be a map, or set of strings
item.description: for_each needs a stable key for every instance, so it accepts only a map or a set of strings. A list is refused because its keys would be positions: remove one item and everything after it would be renumbered and replaced, which is exactly the problem for_each exists to avoid. Variables typed…

item.title: AADSTS50020: User account from identity provider does not exist in tenant
item.description: The person signed in successfully, but with an account that does not belong to the tenant the app sent them to, and they have not been invited as a guest there. Very often the app registration is fine and the URL is wrong: an app meant for any organisation or personal Microsoft accounts is still…

item.title: Airflow: AirflowNotFoundException: The conn_id `postgres_default` isn't defined
item.description: A hook or operator asked for a connection that none of Airflow's backends could supply. Airflow looks in a secrets backend if one is configured, then AIRFLOW_CONN_* environment variables, then the metadata database. The catch is that the lookup happens on the worker running the task, not on the…

item.title: Auth.js: MissingSecret: Please define a `secret`
item.description: Auth.js encrypts its session cookie and signs its tokens with a secret, and in production it will not start without one. Version 5 reads AUTH_SECRET, while NextAuth.js 4 read NEXTAUTH_SECRET, so an upgrade that kept the old variable name is a common cause. In development a fallback is used, which…

item.title: Dart: A value of type 'Future<String>' can't be assigned to a variable of type
item.description: You called an async function and used its result directly, but an async function returns a Future that completes later, not the value itself. Usually an await is missing. item.description: Delta checks every write against the schema stored in the table log and refuses anything that does not fit: a new column, a renamed one, or a type that differs (an int arriving where the table has a long). item.description: DISM needs clean copies of system files to repair the component store or to add a feature such as .NET Framework 3.5, and it could not get them. item.description: The contract reverted with a Solidity custom error, but the ABI you gave ethers does not include that error, so it cannot decode the four byte selector in the data field. item.description: This is the use_build_context_synchronously lint. item.description: Navigator.of(context) walks up the tree from the context you pass, and found no Navigator above it. item.description: wasm32-unknown-unknown has no operating system, so the getrandom crate has no source of randomness to call and refuses to compile rather than guess. item.description: codesign found your signing identity but could not use its private key. item.description: A _pb2.py file was generated by a protoc older than 3.19, and the installed protobuf runtime (4.21 or later) no longer accepts that style of generated code. item.description: The analyser could not match a name in your query to any column available at that point in the plan. item.description: With no serialiser configured, Spring's Redis cache and RedisTemplate fall back to JDK serialisation, which only accepts classes that implement java.io.Serializable. item.description: In Svelte 4 every exported prop could be bound by the parent.
